db/ACTL.function: Enter the basic boundary conditions for elements and the analysis conditions for nonlinear elements. By checking on "Consider Section Stiffness Scale Factor for Stress Calculation" section stiffness variation can be considered for stress calculation.
db/ACTL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Analysis] tab > [Analysis Control] group > [Main Control Data]

db/BMLD.function: Enter beam loads acting on beam elements such as uniformly distributed loads or in-span concentrated loads. Modify or delete previously entered beam loads. Eccentric loads can be applied to beam elements with reference to the GCS or ECS.
db/BMLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Static Loads] group > [Beam Loads] > [ Element]

db/BNGR.function: Define (create, modify & delete) boundary group names to which specific nodes and elements specified with particular boundary conditions are later assigned. In a relatively complicated model for a complex structure, grouping specific nodes and elements assigned with particular boundary conditions becomes handy when the groups of the boundary conditions are to be repeatedly selected.
db/BNGR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Structure] tab > [Group] group > [Group] > [Define Boundary Group]

db/BODF.function: Enter the self-weight of elements included in the model as applied loads, or modify or delete previously entered self-weight. Gen NX uses the volume and density of each element to automatically calculate the self-weight included in the analysis model. The calculated self-weight can be applied in the GCS X, Y and Z-directions in the static analysis.
db/BODF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Create Load Cases] group > [ Self Weight]

db/BTMP.function: Enter the temperature differences between specific locations of beam for thermal stress analysis. The vertical temperature gradient is considered in concrete and steel superstructures with concrete decks, which are subject to temperature difference due to direct sun light and shade.
db/BTMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Temperature] > [Temperature Loads] group > [Beam Section Temperature]

db/CLDR.function: Define the directions of the supports for a display purpose on screen.
db/CLDR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Advanced] group > [Define Label Dir]

db/CLWP.function: Display the internal forces of plate elements along defined cross sectional lines in a graph. This functionality allows us to check the analysis results in a desired direction regardless of the element local coordinate system used in creating plate elements.
db/CLWP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Results] tab > [Type : Analysis Result] > [Result Display] group > [ Forces] > [Plate Cutting Line Diagram]

db/CNLD.function: Enter concentrated nodal loads (Concentrated Forces and Moments), or modify or delete previously entered concentrated loads.
db/CNLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Create Load Cases] group > [Nodal Loads]

db/CONS.function: Restrain the degrees-of-freedom of selected nodes. Replace or remove the support conditions previously defined.
db/CONS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Supports] group > [Define Supports]

db/CUTL.function: Display the internal forces of plate elements along defined cross sectional lines in a graph. This functionality allows us to check the analysis results in a desired direction regardless of the element local coordinate system used in creating plate elements.
db/CUTL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Results] tab > [Type : Analysis Result] > [Result Display] group > [ Forces] > [Plate Cutting Line Diagram]

db/DCON.function: Determine the design code and the special provisions for seismic design (if required) to perform the design or the strength verification for RC members according to the following Concrete Design Criteria: EN 1992-1-1:1994 Eurocode2, Design of concrete structures Part 1 (Eurocode2:04) ENV 1992-1-1:1992 Eurocode2, Design of concrete structures Part 1 (Eurocode2) Ultimate Strength Design, the…
db/DCON.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design] > [Design Input Data] > [Design Code Option]

db/DCTL.function: Select the structural frame type (braced/unbraced) with respect to the global X- and Y-directions. Select the auto-calculation option for the effective buckling length factors for column members.
db/DCTL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Parameters] > [Definition of Frame] From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design] >…

db/DOEL.function: Every time the Automesh function is used to generate a mesh the elements created are placed in a single domain. All the elements belonging to one Domain must have the identical Element Type, Material and Thickness. A Domain can be composed of Sub-Domains and each mesh area that is partitioned when generating a mesh is automatically assigned to a Sub-Domain.
db/DOEL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Node/Element] tab > [Mesh] group > [Domain] > [Define Domain]

db/DRLS.function: Select the desired nodes to be disconnected from Floor Rigid Diaphragms created internally for each floor by the program's Story function.
db/DRLS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Advanced] group > [Diaphragm Disconnect]

db/DSTL.function: Use this function to select the design code to apply for the strength verification of steel members and specify the lateral bracing condition of the structure's horizontal members (beams and girders).
db/DSTL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Code Option]

db/EDMP.function: When the Time Dependent Material Property of structural materials is defined by CEB-FIP, the geometric shape dimension (h) is revised here. The dimension (h) is applied to automatically calculate the time dependent property of the elements that used the defined material.
db/EDMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Material Properties] group > [Change Property]

db/EFCT.function: Initial forces, which are defined in Load > Initial Forces > Small Displacement > Initial Element Forces, are added to a specific load case. Or initial member forces are generated from Member forces due to specific load cases/combinations.
db/EFCT.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Misc.] tab > [Type : Initial Forces] > [Initial Forces] group > [Small Displacement] > [Initial Forces Control Data]

db/ELEM.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Node/Element] tab > [General] group > [Create] > [Create Element] Shortcut key: [Alt]+1

db/ELNK.function: Create or remove elastic links. Two nodes are connected by an elastic link and its stiffness is defined by the user.
db/ELNK.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] > [Link] > [Elastic Link]

db/EPMT.function: Specify a plastic material model for material nonlinear analysis. Plastic Material Models Tresca & Von Mises Appropriate for ductile metals, which exhibit Plastic Incompressibility Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager Appropriate for brittle materials such as concrete, rock and soils, which exhibit the behavior of volumetric plastic straining Masonry Appropriate for the elastic analysis finding the crack…
db/EPMT.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Material Properties] group > [Plastic Material]

db/EPST.function: Add static earth pressure to spatial structures of general shapes. When a line element that forms a closed area is selected, the static earth pressure of the area is applied to each node as a nodal load.
db/EPST.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Lateral] group > [Earth Pressure] > [Static Earth Pressure]

db/ESSF.function: Apply scale factors to the cross-sectional linear elements (Truss, Tension-only, Compression-only, Cable, Gap, Hook & Beam Elements). Specific stiffness of specific member types may be reduced such as the case where the flexural stiffness of lintel beams and walls may require reduction to reflect cracked sections of concrete Select a boundary group in which the Element Stiffness Scale Factors…
db/ESSF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Section Properties] group > [Scale Factor] > [Element Stiffness Scale Factor]

db/ETMP.function: Specify element temperatures, or modify or delete previously defined temperatures for thermal analysis. (refer to "System Temperature")
db/ETMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Temperature] > [Temperature Loads] group > [Element Temp.]

db/EXLD.feature_name: External Type Load Case for Pretension
db/EXLD.function: Apply the pretension load of truss elements as an external type. In the general static analysis, this version regards the pretension load as an internal type, but using this function, the pretension load can be entered as an external type. P-Delta Analysis can be executed at the same time.
db/EXLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Prestress] > [Prestress Loads] group > [ External Type LoadCase]

db/FBLA.function: Enter floor loads within a "closed" planar polygon. The floor loads are converted into line beam loads or in-span, concentrated beam loads applied to the top of wall, plate or beam elements. When the floor load and shape are typical for each story, as in buildings, it is very convenient to use the simultaneous load using Copy Floor Load function.
db/FBLA.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Advanced] group > [Assign Floor Loads] > [Assign Floor Loads]

db/FBLD.function: Define the floor load cases and the corresponding floor loads. The floor loads defined here are applied to the structure by the Assign Floor Loads command. Although the floor loads such as dead, live, roof and snow loads have different values, they share the common loading areas.
db/FBLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Advanced] group > [Assign Floor Loads] > [Define Floor Load Type]

db/FIBR.function: In order to carry out a nonlinear analysis using fiber elements, beam cross-sections are appropriately divided into fiber cells. Such fiber cells are assigned various nonlinear material properties representing stress-strain hysteresis models for concrete, steel, etc. For a reinforced concrete structure, cover concrete, core concrete, reinforcing steel, etc. can be assigned to the sections.
db/FIBR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Inelastic Properties] group > [Inelastic Material] > [Fiber Division of Section]

db/FIMP.function: Stress-strain relationships between reinforcing steel and concrete are defined to carry out inelastic time history analysis using Fiber Elements. Each model is unique based on the proponents and specifications.
db/FIMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Inelastic Properties] group > [Inelastic Material] > [Inelastic Material Properties]

db/FRLS.function: Enter the end release conditions (Hinge, Sliding, Roller Joint and Partial Fixity) at both ends of beam elements, or replace or remove previously entered end release conditions. Beam End Offsets can be specified in conjunction with (Beam End Offsets).
db/FRLS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Release/Offset] group > [Beam End Release]

db/GRDP.feature_name: Group Damping : Element Mass & Stiffness Proportional
db/GRDP.function: Group Damping is used to assign different damping ratios resulting from time history analysis to different element and boundary groups. When the materials, vibration control devices or vibration isolators in a structure have different damping ratios, elements with different damping ratios can be assigned to different Element Groups.
db/GRDP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Damping] group > [Group Damping] > [Element Mass Stiffness Proportional]

db/GRUP.function: Define (create, modify & delete) structure group names to which specific nodes and elements are later assigned. In a relatively complicated model for a complex structure, grouping specific elements (ie, saving selection of certain elements) becomes handy when the groups of elements are to be repeatedly selected.
db/GRUP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Structure] tab > [Group] group > [Group] > [Structure] Shortcut key: [Ctrl]+[F1]

db/GSPR.function: Enter general spring support with 6x6 coupled matrix for stiffness, damping and mass, which includes the components related to other degrees-of-freedom with respect to GCS or node's local coordinate system for selected nodes. Replace or delete previously defined general spring support. Define the general spring support matrix first to enter the general spring supports.
db/GSPR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Springs] group > [General Spring] > [General Spring Supports]

db/GSTP.function: Define the values of General Spring Support with 6x6 coupled matrix for stiffness, damping and mass to represent the dynamic properties of pile-soil system.
db/GSTP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Springs] group > [General Spring] > [Define General Spring Type]

db/GTMP.function: Enter the temperature differences between the tops and bottoms of beam or plate elements for thermal stress analysis. Modify or delete previously entered temperature differences. The temperature gradient analysis is applicable for elements with bending stiffness such as beam and plate elements.
db/GTMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Temperature] > [Temperature Loads] group > [Temperature Gradient]

db/IEHC.function: This is a dialog box to automatically generate a fiber model for the inelastic analysis. To create a fiber model, the location of the reference section and mesh size are set in this dialog box.
db/IEHC.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Inelastic Properties] group > [Inel. Control Data] > [Inel. Control Data]

db/IEHG.function: Assign or delete inelastic hinge properties to elements.
db/IEHG.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Inelastic Properties] group > [Inelastic Hinge] > [Assign Inelastic Hinge Properties]

db/IFGS.function: Enter initial axial forces into selected members for geometric stiffness calculation. When cable elements are used, the self-weight of the cables should be inputted so that it can be considered in the analysis.
db/IFGS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Misc.] tab > [Type : Initial Forces] > [Initial Forces] > [Large Displacement] > [Initial Forces for Geometric Stiffness]

db/IMFM.function: Stress-strain relationships between reinforcing steel and concrete are defined to carry out inelastic time history analysis using Fiber Elements. Each model is unique based on the proponents and specifications.
db/IMFM.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Inelastic Properties] group > [Inelastic Material] > [Inelastic Material Properties]

db/INMF.function: Enter the member forces in the structure due to external loads. The member forces are calculated using Initial Force Control Data. Initial forces, which are entered here, can be added to a specific load case, or initial member forces are generated from member forces due to specific load cases/combinations, as controlled from Load > Initial Force > Small Displacement > Initial Force Control Data.
db/INMF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] group > [Type : Misc.] > [Initial Forces] group > [Small Displacement] > [Initial Element Forces]

db/LDGR.function: Define (create, modify & delete) load group names to which loaded nodes and elements are later assigned. In a relatively complicated model for a complex structure, grouping specifically loaded nodes and elements becomes handy when the groups of the loads are to be repeatedly selected.
db/LDGR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Structure] tab > [Group] group > [Group] > [Define Load Group]

db/LENG.function: Enter the unbraced lengths for buckling about the strong (y-axis) and weak (z-axis) axes of the selected compression members. Enter the laterally unbraced length for the compression flange of a member bent about its weak axis.
db/LENG.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Parameters] > [Unbraced Length (L,Lb)] From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design]…

db/LLAN.function: Enter the traffic (line) lanes for moving load analysis.
db/LLAN.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Traffic Line Lanes]

db/LLANCH.function: Enter the traffic (line) lanes for moving load analysis.
db/LLANCH.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Traffic Line Lanes]

db/LLANID.function: Enter the traffic (line) lanes for moving load analysis.
db/LLANID.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Traffic Line Lanes]

db/LLANOP.function: Enter the traffic (line) lanes for moving load analysis.
db/LLANOP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Traffic Line Lanes]

db/LLANTR.function: Enter the traffic (line) lanes for moving load analysis.
db/LLANTR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Traffic Line Lanes]

db/LTOM.function: Convert the values of the vertical components of the entered loads (loads acting in GCS (-)Z-direction) to masses and enter them as lumped mass data.
db/LTOM.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Masses] group > [Masses] > [ Loads to Masses]

db/LTSR.function: Use this function to enter the limiting slenderness ratios for members subjected to axial compressive and tensile forces.
db/LTSR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Parameters] > [Limiting Slenderness Ratio] From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : SRC…

db/MADO.function: Every time the Automesh function is used to generate a mesh the elements created are placed in a single domain. All the elements belonging to one Domain must have the identical Element Type, Material and Thickness. A Domain can be composed of Sub-Domains and each mesh area that is partitioned when generating a mesh is automatically assigned to a Sub-Domain.
db/MADO.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Node/Element] tab > [Mesh] group > [Domain] > [Define Domain]

db/MATD.function: Use this function to modify a part of the steel rebar and concrete material property data, entered during the creation of the analysis model, or to change the material property data. Modifications that are made here will not affect the analysis results, but will only be used for automatic design and strength verification.
db/MATD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Modify Concrete Material]

db/MATL.function: Enter the isotropic and orthotropic material properties. The user should enter the orthotropic material in User Defined Material.
db/MATL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Material Properties] group > [Material Properties]

db/MBTP.function: Enter the type of members used in the design of steel and RC members.
db/MBTP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Parameters] > [Modify Member Type] From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design] >…

db/MCON.function: Constrain a specific node to subordinate to the movements of certain nodes. Here, the specific subordinate node is referred to as a constraint node, and the nodes to which the specific node is subordinated are referred to as independent nodes. The relationship between the constraint node and the independent nodes is established. Constraining translational displacement Eq.
db/MCON.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Advanced] group > [Linear Constraints]

db/MEMB.function: A single Member can be assigned when the member is consisted of a number of line elements (beam elements or truss elements).
db/MEMB.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : Steel Design] > [Design Input Data] group > [Design Parameters] > [ Member Assignment] From the Main Menu select [Design] tab > [Type : RC Design] >…

db/MLSP.feature_name: Lane Supports(Negative Moments at Interior Piers)
db/MLSP.function: Assign the elements constituting a multiple span being considered for moving load analysis using traffic lane loads. When a support is defined by the function, Gen NX automatically places concentrated loads of equivalent magnitudes to the uniformly distributed loads on the spans each side of the support in addition to the uniformly distributed loads.
db/MLSP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Advanced] group > [Lane Supports] > [Lane Support-Nega. Moments]

db/MLSR.feature_name: Lane Supports(Negative Moments at Interior Piers)
db/MLSR.function: Assign the elements constituting a multiple span being considered for moving load analysis using traffic lane loads. When a support is defined by the function, Gen NX automatically places concentrated loads of equivalent magnitudes to the uniformly distributed loads on the spans each side of the support in addition to the uniformly distributed loads.
db/MLSR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Advanced] group > [Lane Supports] > [Lane Support-Nega. Moments]

db/MVCD.function: Prior to defining moving load, Code must be selected first from Moving Load Analysis Data > Moving Load.
db/MVCD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Code] group > [Moving Load Code]

db/MVLD.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDBS.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDBS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDCH.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDCH.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDEU.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDEU.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDID.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDID.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDPL.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDPL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/MVLDTR.function: Use the entered vehicle load classes and the traffic lanes to create moving load cases.
db/MVLDTR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Moving Load] > [Moving Load Analysis Data] group > [Moving Load Cases]

db/NBOF.function: Convert Nodal Mass, Load to Mass and Structure Mass assigned to a selected node to a nodal (body) force in a specific direction. The scale factor can be applied in each direction. This is useful to apply load according to the mass distribution to each node in the pushover analysis.
db/NBOF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Masses] group > [Masses] > [ Nodal Body Force]

db/NLLP.function: Add, modify or delete the properties of general link elements. General Link elements are used for modeling damping devices, base isolators, compression or tension-only elements, plastic hinges, soil springs, etc. General Link elements can be assigned linear and nonlinear properties using spring properties. The procedure for boundary nonlinear dynamic analysis is shown below. Procedure Menu 1.
db/NLLP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] > [Link] > [General Link] > [General Link Properties]

db/NLNK.function: Create or delete general link elements, each linking two nodes.
db/NLNK.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] > [Link] > [General Link] > [General Link]

db/NMAS.function: Enter lumped mass data (Lumped Translation Mass/Rotational Mass Moment of Inertia) for nodes, or modify or delete previously entered nodal masses.
db/NMAS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Masses] group > [Masses] > [Nodal Masses]

db/NODE.function: Create a new node or create a set of nodes by copying the node simultaneously.
db/NODE.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Node/Element] tab > [General] group > [Create] > [Create Node]

db/NPLN.function: Assign names to specific planes. When using Selection, simply recall the name of a plane on which relevant nodes and elements are located. Named planes also come in handy for Activity. Named Plane helps the user visualize and maneuver complex 3D structures. Models can be handled by 2D unit frames or by sections in the in/output processes.
db/NPLN.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [View] tab > [View] group > [Named] > [Named Plane]

db/NSPR.function: Enter Spring Stiffness of selected nodes in each direction of GCS or nodal local coordinate system. Replace or remove previously defined spring stiffness.
db/NSPR.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Springs] group > [Point Spring]

db/NTMP.function: Enter nodal temperatures for thermal stress analysis, and modify or delete previously entered temperatures. (Refer to "System Temperature")
db/NTMP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Temperature] > [Temperature Loads] group > [Nodal Temperatures]

db/OFFS.function: Define Rigid End Offset Distance or take into account the Joint Eccentricity with respect to GCS or element's local coordinate system at both ends of beam elements. Beam End Offsets can be specified in conjunction with (Beam End Release).
db/OFFS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Release/Offset] group > [Beam End Offsets]

db/PJCF.function: Register the general project information (project name, user name, etc.).
db/PJCF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Project] tab > [Management] group > [Project Information]

db/PNLA.function: Apply the plane loads defined in (Plane Load Type) to any specific locations on plate or solid elements. Plane Load is the function to assign specific load type defined by the user on plate or solid elements. This function is especially useful for assigning specific load type to various locations such as equipment load.
db/PNLA.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Pressure Load] group > [Assign Plane Loads] > [Assign Plane Loads]

db/PNLD.function: Define types and magnitudes of Plane Loads. The Plane Loads defined by this feature are applied to the structure through the Assign Plane Loads feature. The Plane Loads can be applied to any specific locations on plate and solid elements, which constitute an analysis model. This capability alleviates the cumbersome tasks of locating nodes where loads are applied.
db/PNLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Pressure Load] group > [Assign Plane Loads] > [Define Plane Load Type]

db/POLC.function: Define load cases for pushover analysis.
db/POLC.menu_path: From the nain nenu, select [Poshover] tab > [Load Case] group > [Load Case]

db/POSL.function: In Gen NX, the automatic data entry of equivalent static seismic loads according to various standards is applicable for common buildings where each story can be defined and can reasonably act as a rigid diaphragm. Procedure of the automatic data entry of static seismic loads 1. Model the structure.
db/POSL.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Load] > [Lateral] group > [Seismic Loads]

db/POSP.function: Set soil properties for the calculation of static earth pressure.
db/POSP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Lateral] group > [Earth Pressure] > [Parameters of Soil Properties]

db/PRES.function: Apply pressure loads to the faces or edges of plate, plane stress, plane strain, axisymmetric or solid elements. Modify or delete previously entered loads. The pressure loads are entered as either a uniform pressure or a linearly distributed pressure. The pressure is then converted into equivalent nodal forces in the program.
db/PRES.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Pressure Load] group > [Pressure Loads] > [Assign Pressure Loads]

db/PRLS.function: Enter the nodal connection conditions (Hinge, Fixed Joint) for plate elements, or replace or remove previously entered end release conditions.
db/PRLS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Release/Offset] group > [Plate End Release]

db/PRST.function: Enter pre-stress loads for beams, or modify or delete previously entered loads. The concept of defining the pre-stress loads in beams is illustrated below. The cable drape is located on a 2-D curve passing through 3 eccentric points. It is assumed that the eccentric points are on the beam element's local x-z plane.
db/PRST.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Prestress] > [Prestress Loads] group > [ Prestress Beam Loads]

db/PSLT.function: Define the pressure load cases and the corresponding pressure loads. The pressure loads defined here are applied to the structure by the Assign Pressure Loads command. Although the pressure loads such as dead, live, roof and snow loads have different values, they share the common loading areas.
db/PSLT.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Pressure Load] group > [Pressure Loads] > [Define Pressure Load Type]

db/PSSF.function: Apply scale factors to the cross-sectional properties of plate elements. In-plane shear and bending stiffness of specific plate elements may be reduced to reflect cracked sections of concrete walls and slabs. For unstructured meshes, scale factors can be applied to the user-defined direction. Note.
db/PSSF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Section Properties] group > [Scale Factor] > [Plate Stiffness Scale Factor]

db/PTNS.function: Specify pretension loads for Truss elements or tension-only elements (hook & cable). Or, modify or delete previously specified loads. This load cannot be used for performing analysis with materials having nonlinear properties.
db/PTNS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Prestress] > [Prestress Loads] group > [ Pretension Loads]

db/PZEF.function: Automatically consider the stiffness effects of the Panel Zone where column members and girder members (horizontal elements connected to columns) of steel structures are connected. Panel Zone Effects are reflected in the beam elements. Column members are recognized as beam elements parallel to the GCS Z-axis and beam members are recognized as beam elements on the GCS X-Y plane.
db/PZEF.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Advanced] group > [Panel Zone Effects]

db/RIGD.function: Constrain certain degrees-of-freedom of Slave Nodes to a Master Node. If a degree-of-freedom of a particular slave node is constrained to a master node by this command, "Rigid Link" relationship is established for the relevant degree-of-freedom.

db/SBDO.function: A Sub-Domain is the unit area of mesh elements. When generating a mesh, the entire mesh area is the Domain and the mesh elements that partition the mesh are the Sub-Domains. A Sub-Domain can be defined automatically when a mesh is generated or can be defined directly from the Define Sub-Domain dialog box. Sub-Domains are automatically assigned numerical names when created (1, 2, 3....).
db/SBDO.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Node/Element] tab > [Mesh] group > [Domain] > [Define Sub-Domain]

db/SDHY.function: Add, modify or delete the properties of Hysteretic Isolator (MSS) elements.

db/SDIS.function: Add, modify or delete the properties of Isolator elements.
db/SDIS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Advanced] group > [Seismic Device] > [Isolator (MSS)]

db/SDSP.function: Enter specified (forced) nodal displacements, or modify or delete previously entered specified (forced) displacements.
db/SDSP.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Static Loads] group > [Specified Displ.]

db/SDST.function: Add, modify or delete the properties of Steel Damper elements.

db/SECF.function: Apply scale factors to the cross-sectional properties of linear elements (Truss, Tension-only, Compression-only, Cable, Gap, Hook & Beam Elements). db/SINF.function: Use plate elements to represent additional surfaces for which an influence surface analysis is to be carried out. When influence surface analysis results are required for additional surfaces beyond the range of the traffic surface lane, plate elements are used for the moving load analysis.

db/SKEW.function: Declare a local coordinate system for selected nodes to enter boundary conditions or produce output for reactions.

db/SLANCH.function: Enter the traffic surface lanes for moving load analysis.

db/SPFC.function: Enter spectral data for response spectrum analysis. Response Spectrum Analysis calculates modal responses using the natural periods obtained by Eigenvalue analysis. Range of the natural periods obtained from Eigenvalue analysis

db/SSPS.function: Enter spring stiffness per unit supporting area of planar or solid elements to create elastic spring supports. Elastic Link elements may be created simultaneously. This function is mainly used to define a number of elastic supports on surfaces represented by the modulus of spring.
db/SSPS.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Boundary] tab > [Springs] group > [Surface Spring]

db/STLD.function: Define static load cases, or modify or delete previously defined load cases. Static analysis is carried out for each static load case entered by this function. The analysis results can be interactively combined in "Combinations". Apply this feature to assign the load cases necessary to form the geometric stiffness matrix in the P-Delta or buckling analysis.
db/STLD.menu_path: From the Main Menu Select [Load] tab > [Type : Static Loads] > [Create Load Cases] group > [Static Load Cases] Shortcut key : [F9] Click the ...

db/STMP.function: When the temperature of the entire structure varies from an initial (reference) temperature to a set temperature (final temperature) for thermal stress analysis, enter the final or system temperature. Because the positions of the stories are defined using the GCS Z-axis coordinates, the floor planes of the building must inevitably be parallel to GCS X-Y plane. db/STYP.function: Enter the type of and the basic data for structural analysis.

db/TDCS.function: Specify a part of composite section, through which a selected tendon profile is passing. This data is used to calculate the net area of prestressed concrete section. Note 1 If this is not specified, it is assumed that tendon profiles pass through Part1.

db/TDGR.function: Define (add, modify & delete) Tendon Group names to which specific tendons are later assigned. db/TDME.function: Define Compressive Strength of concrete or the change of modulus of elasticity to reflect the variation of modulus of elasticity with time. db/TDME.menu_path: From the Main Menu select [Properties] tab > [Material Properties] group > [Time Dependent Material] > [Comp. Strength]

db/TDMF.function: The user directly defines the time dependent material properties (creep, shrinkage, and relaxation) of concrete. db/THIK.function: Enter thickness data for planar elements (plate element, plane stress element).

db/THIS.function: Define the conditions and required control data for time history analysis. The procedure for carrying out a time history analysis is outlined below. 1. Enter the mass data in the analysis model using the various mass input functions provided in the Model > Masses menu. 2.

db/ULFC.function: Use optimization techniques to determine the optimal load factors that satisfy the specific constraints of a structure.
